as_told.title: Stubblebine's PK search and the 'Did you kill my computers' recruitment

plain: In the 1980s the Army general Albert Stubblebine brought an Army sergeant named Lyn Buchanan to Fort Meade, Maryland, to join a unit that trained soldiers in remote viewing, meaning describing faraway places with the mind alone. Buchanan tells Michels the general was looking for people who could move or affect things by thought, and once got up in his face and asked, "Did you kill my computers with your mind?" He mentions the book The Men Who Stare at Goats while telling it, and if his story is true, the Army really was searching its ranks for psychic talent.
